(* pool. A commit only succeeds if the instance's snapshotted version     *)
(* still matches the live version, which is exactly what prevents a       *)
(* stale snapshot from silently overwriting -- losing -- another update.  *)
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Instance, PoolSize, MaxLog

ASSUME PoolSize \in Nat /\ MaxLog \in Nat

VARIABLES count, version, localCount, localVersion, log

vars == <<count, version, localCount, localVersion, log>>

Kind == {"hold", "release", "reset"}
LogEntry == [kind: Kind, val: 0..PoolSize]

TypeOK ==
    /\ count \in 0..PoolSize
    /\ version \in 0..MaxLog
    /\ localCount \in [Instance -> 0..PoolSize]
    /\ localVersion \in [Instance -> 0..MaxLog]
    /\ log \in Seq(LogEntry)

Init ==
    /\ count = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ localCount = [i \in Instance |-> 0]
    /\ localVersion = [i \in Instance |-> 0]
    /\ log = <<>>

Snapshot(i) ==
    /\ localCount' = [localCount EXCEPT ![i] = count]
    /\ localVersion' = [localVersion EXCEPT ![i] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, version, log>>

Hold(i) ==
    /\ localVersion[i] = version
    /\ localCount[i] < PoolSize
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ count' = localCount[i] + 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ log' = Append(log, [kind |-> "hold", val |-> localCount[i] + 1])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<localCount, localVersion>>

Release(i) ==
    /\ localVersion[i] = version
    /\ localCount[i] > 0
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ count' = localCount[i] - 1
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ log' = Append(log, [kind |-> "release", val |-> localCount[i] - 1])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<localCount, localVersion>>

AdminReset ==
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLog
    /\ count' = 0
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ log' = Append(log, [kind |-> "reset", val |-> 0])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<localCount, localVersion>>

Next_ == (\E i \in Instance : Snapshot(i) \/ Hold(i) \/ Release(i)) \/ AdminReset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next_]_vars

EntryOK(k) ==
    LET prevVal == IF k = 1 THEN 0 ELSE log[k - 1].val
    IN  IF log[k].kind = "hold" THEN log[k].val = prevVal + 1
        ELSE IF log[k].kind = "release" THEN log[k].val = prevVal - 1
        ELSE log[k].val = 0

(* Every history entry is exactly one step from its predecessor: no CAS   *)
(* ever commits against a value it did not actually observe, so no       *)
(* instance's update is ever silently lost underneath another's.         *)
NoLostUpdate == \A k \in 1..Len(log) : EntryOK(k)

To place a new hold, an instance computes count-plus-one from its own snapshot and compare-and-swaps it into the shared record, but only if the shared record's live version number still equals the version number it snapshotted; a successful swap also bumps the shared version by one and appends the resulting count, tagged as a hold, onto a shared append-only history.     /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, using>>

LeaveFleet(r) ==
    /\ r \in active
    /\ leader # r
    /\ Cardinality(active) > 1
    /\ active' = active \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, using>>

Elect(r) ==
    /\ r \in active
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ leader' = r
    /\ term' = (term + 1) % MaxTerm
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, using>>

Fail ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ using' = [using EXCEPT ![leader] = FALSE]
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, active>>

StartUsing(r) ==
    /\ leader = r
    /\ ~using[r]
    /\ using' = [using EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, active>>

StopUsing(r) ==
    /\ leader = r
    /\ using[r]
    /\ using' = [using EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, active>>

Next_ ==
    \/ \E r \in Robot : JoinFleet(r) \/ LeaveFleet(r) \/ Elect(r) \/ StartUsing(r) \/ StopUsing(r)
    \/ Fail

ElectAny == \E r \in Robot : Elect(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next_]_vars /\ WF_vars(ElectAny)

(* At most one robot ever operates the shared docking arm at once. *)
MutualExclusion == Cardinality({r \in Robot : using[r]}) <= 1

(* Whenever the fleet is leaderless, it eventually elects a new leader. *)
EventualLeader == (leader = NoLeader) ~> (leader # NoLeader)

nl: A warehouse robot fleet elects one of its currently active members as leader, and only the current leader may operate the single shared docking arm that loads pallets onto the conveyor -- every other robot, active or not, must stay off the arm entirely. The fleet's roster of active robots is not fixed: a robot can join the active roster at any time, and an active robot that is not the current leader can also leave the active roster at any time, so long as at least one active robot always remains to keep the fleet running -- capacity rises and falls as robots come and go. Leader election only runs while the fleet is currently leaderless: any active robot can be elected, which advances the fleet's election-term counter and installs that robot as the new leader. The leader can fail and step down at any moment, which immediately clears the docking arm (in case it was using the arm at the time) and leaves the fleet leaderless until the next election. While it is the leader, a robot may start operating the docking arm, and it may later stop operating it. The six actions in this system are: a robot joining the active roster, a non-leader active robot leaving the active roster, electing a new leader from among the active robots while the fleet is leaderless, the leader failing and stepping down, the leader starting to operate the docking arm, and the leader stopping operating the docking arm. SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one robot is ever operating the docking arm at the same time. LIVENESS PROPERTY: whenever the fleet is leaderless, it eventually elects a new leader.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Guests, Doors, MaxGuests, NoG

VARIABLES coarseHolder, fineHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors, ackInflight

vars == <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

\* A smart-home door lock network issues temporary guest credentials using
\* hierarchical locking: a single coarse home-wide lock admits at most one
\* guest-issuance transaction at a time, and reserves the transaction's
\* capacity slot immediately; a fine per-door lock is then taken briefly
\* while the credential is written into each door's local memory. Each
\* door's write-completion acknowledgement travels through an unordered
\* buffer, so acks can be delivered out of order or after the issuance
\* that sent them has already been cancelled (the twist); ProcessAck only
\* credits a door's write toward the CURRENT coarse holder, so a stale ack
\* from a cancelled issuance can never be misattributed. CapacityBounded
\* checks that the number of active guest credentials never exceeds the
\* home's configured limit.

Init ==
  /\ coarseHolder = NoG
  /\ fineHolder = [d \in Doors |-> NoG]
  /\ activeGuests = {}
  /\ writtenDoors = {}
  /\ ackInflight = {}

\* Reserves the capacity slot as soon as an issuance transaction begins --
\* this is the single point that enforces the bound, regardless of how
\* the per-door writes and their acks are later interleaved or reordered.
StartIssue(g) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = NoG
  /\ g \notin activeGuests
  /\ Cardinality(activeGuests) < MaxGuests
  /\ coarseHolder' = g
  /\ activeGuests' = activeGuests \cup {g}
  /\ writtenDoors' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineHolder, ackInflight>>

AcquireFineWrite(g, d) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = g
  /\ fineHolder[d] = NoG
  /\ d \notin writtenDoors
  /\ fineHolder' = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![d] = g]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

ReleaseFineAndAck(g, d) ==
  /\ fineHolder[d] = g
  /\ fineHolder' = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![d] = NoG]
  /\ ackInflight' = ackInflight \cup {<<g, d>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors>>

\* A door's write ack arrives, possibly late or out of order. It only
\* counts toward completion if the sender is still the live coarse
\* holder -- a reordered ack for a since-cancelled issuance is dropped.
ProcessAck(g, d) ==
  /\ <<g, d>> \in ackInflight
  /\ ackInflight' = ackInflight \ {<<g, d>>}
  /\ IF coarseHolder = g
       THEN writtenDoors' = writtenDoors \cup {d}
       ELSE writtenDoors' = writtenDoors
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, activeGuests>>

FinishIssue(g) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = g
  /\ writtenDoors = Doors
  /\ coarseHolder' = NoG
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineHolder, activeGuests, writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

\* An issuance can be abandoned before every door has been written (e.g.
\* the guest declined). Its capacity slot is released immediately, but
\* any of its acks already in flight are left untouched -- they will
\* later be safely dropped by ProcessAck's staleness check.
CancelIssue(g) ==
  /\ coarseHolder = g
  /\ writtenDoors # Doors
  /\ coarseHolder' = NoG
  /\ activeGuests' = activeGuests \ {g}
  /\ fineHolder' = [d \in Doors |-> IF fineHolder[d] = g THEN NoG ELSE fineHolder[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

Revoke(g) ==
  /\ g \in activeGuests
  /\ coarseHolder # g
  /\ activeGuests' = activeGuests \ {g}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, writtenDoors, ackInflight>>

Next ==
  \/ \E g \in Guests : StartIssue(g)
  \/ \E g \in Guests, d \in Doors : AcquireFineWrite(g, d)
  \/ \E g \in Guests, d \in Doors : ReleaseFineAndAck(g, d)
  \/ \E g \in Guests, d \in Doors : ProcessAck(g, d)
  \/ \E g \in Guests : FinishIssue(g)
  \/ \E g \in Guests : CancelIssue(g)
  \/ \E g \in Guests : Revoke(g)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityBounded == Cardinality(activeGuests) <= MaxGuests

nl:
A smart-home door lock network issues temporary guest access credentials across all of a home's doors at once, using a hierarchical locking scheme. A single coarse, home-wide lock admits only one guest-issuance transaction at a time and immediately reserves that transaction's slot against the home's configured limit on simultaneously active guest credentials. Once admitted, the transaction takes a fine-grained lock on each individual door in turn to write the new credential into that door's local memory, then releases the door's lock and sends an acknowledgement back to the hub confirming the write.

The twist is that these per-door write acknowledgements travel through an unordered network buffer, so they can arrive late or out of order -- and in particular, an acknowledgement can still be in flight when its own issuance transaction gets cancelled (for example, if the guest declines partway through setup). The hub handles this by only crediting an acknowledgement toward an issuance's progress if the sender is still the currently active coarse-lock holder; a stale acknowledgement that arrives after its issuance has already been cancelled is simply dropped rather than mistakenly counted.

The full action set is: StartIssue(g), where guest g's issuance transaction takes the coarse lock, provided no other issuance is in progress and the home is under its configured limit on active credentials -- this is the point where g's capacity slot is reserved; AcquireFineWrite(g, d), where the current coarse-lock holder g takes the fine lock on door d to write g's credential there; ReleaseFineAndAck(g, d), where g releases door d's fine lock and sends the write's acknowledgement into the network; ProcessAck(g, d), where a previously sent acknowledgement from g for door d is delivered -- it counts toward g's progress only if g is still the current coarse-lock holder, and is otherwise dropped as stale; FinishIssue(g), where g's transaction completes once every door has been written, releasing the coarse lock; CancelIssue(g), where g's transaction is abandoned before every door was written, releasing the coarse lock and g's reserved capacity slot immediately; and Revoke(g), where a guest g with an already-active credential has it revoked, freeing its capacity slot for reuse.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of simultaneously active guest credentials never exceeds the home's configured limit, no matter how the per-door write acknowledgements are delayed, reordered, or rendered stale by a cancelled issuance.
